question.text: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y}$ given that $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y} = -\dfrac{xy}{x^2+y^2}.$
question.explanation:
To find $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y}$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y} &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(-\dfrac{xy}{x^2+y^2}\right) \\[5pt] &= -y \cdot \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(\dfrac{x}{x^2+y^2}\right) \\[5pt] &= -y \left(\dfrac{1}{x^2+y^2} -\dfrac{2x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2}\right) \\[5pt] &= -y\left(\dfrac{(x^2+y^2)-2x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2}\right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{y(x^2-y^2)}{(x^2+y^2)^2} \end{align*}

question.text: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x^2}$ given that $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial x} =2 xye^{(x^2+y^2)}.$
question.explanation:
To find $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x^2}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial x}$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x^2} &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial x} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\partial }{\partial x} \left(2 xye^{(x^2+y^2)}\right)\\[5pt] &=2y\cdot \dfrac{\partial }{\partial x} \left( xe^{(x^2+y^2)} \right)\\[5pt] &= 2y\cdot\left(e^{(x^2+y^2)}+2x^2e^{(x^2+y^2)}\right) \\[5pt] &=2y(1+2x^2)e^{(x^2+y^2)} \end{align*}

question.text: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y}$ given that $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y} = \dfrac{3y^2}{\sqrt{2x+y^3}}.$
question.explanation:
To find $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y}$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y} &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left( \dfrac{3y^2}{\sqrt{2x+y^3}} \right) \\[5pt] &= 3y^2 \cdot \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left((2x+y^3)^{-1/2}\right) \\[5pt] &= 3y^2 \left( -\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot (2x+y^3)^{-3/2} \cdot 2 \right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{3y^2}{\sqrt{(2x+y^3)^3}} \end{align*}

question.text: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y}$ given that $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y} = x^2y\cos{(xy^2)}.$
question.explanation:
To find $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y}$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y} &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(x^2y\cos{(xy^2)}\right) \\[5pt] &= y \cdot \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(x^2\cos{(xy^2)}\right) \\[5pt] &= y \cdot(2x\cos{(xy^2)} - x^2 y^2\sin{(xy^2)}) \\[5pt] &= 2xy\cos{(xy^2)}-x^2y^3\sin{(xy^2)} \end{align*}

question.text: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y}$ given that $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y} = -\dfrac{2x^2+y}{y^3}.$
question.explanation:
To find $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y}$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y} &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(-\dfrac{2x^2+y}{y^3}\right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{y^3} \cdot \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(2x^2+y\right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{y^3} (4x) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{4x}{y^3} \end{align*}

To find $f_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $f_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} f_{xx}(x,y)&=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(f_x(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(-\dfrac{y}{x^2+y^2}\right) \\[5pt] &= -y\cdot\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(\dfrac{1}{x^2+y^2}\right)\\[5pt] &= -y\cdot\left(-\dfrac{2x}{(x^2+y^2)^2}\right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2xy}{(x^2+y^2)^2} \end{align}

To find $f_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $f_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} f_{yy}(x,y)&=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(f_y(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(\dfrac{x}{x^2+y^2}\right) \\[5pt] &=x\cdot \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(\dfrac{1}{x^2+y^2}\right) \\[5pt] &= x\cdot\left(-\dfrac{2y}{(x^2+y^2)^2}\right)\\[3pt] &=-\dfrac{2xy}{(x^2+y^2)^2} \end{align}

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} f_{xx}(x,y) + f_{yy}(x,y) &= \dfrac{2xy}{(x^2+y^2)^2} - \dfrac{2xy}{(x^2+y^2)^2} =0 . \end{align*}

\begin{align*} g_{xy}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y}\left( g_x(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac {\partial}{\partial y}\left( (x^2+y)e^{y^2}\right) \\[5pt] &=e^{y^2}+2y(x^2+y)e^{y^2}\\[5pt] &=\left(1+2y^2+2x^2y\right)e^{y^2} \end{align*}

To find $g_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $g_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} g_{xx}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x}\left( g_x(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac {\partial}{\partial x}\left( (x^2+y)e^{y^2}\right) \\[5pt] &=2xe^{y^2} \end{align*}

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} g_{xy}(x,y) + g_{xx}(x,y) &=\left(1+2y^2+2x^2y\right)e^{y^2}+ 2xe^{y^2} \\[3pt] &=\left(1+2x+2y^2+2x^2y\right)e^{y^2} . \end{align*}

example.title: Computing Expressions Involving Second-Order Partial Derivatives

\begin{align} f_{xy}(x,y)&=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(f_x(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(-\dfrac{e^y}{x^2}\right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{e^y}{x^2} \end{align}

To find $f_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $f_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} f_{yx}(x,y)&=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(f_y(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(\dfrac{e^y}{x}\right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{e^y}{x^2} \end{align}

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} f_{xy}(x,y) + f_{yx}(x,y) &= -\dfrac{e^y}{x^2} -\dfrac{e^y}{x^2} = -\dfrac{2e^y}{x^2} . \end{align*}

example.title: Computing Expressions Involving Second-Order Partial Derivatives

question.explanation:
To find $f_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $f_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} f_{xy}(x,y)&=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(f_x(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(x\cos{(x^2-y^2)}\right) \\[5pt] &= x\cdot\left(-\sin{(x^2 - y^2)}\cdot (-2y)\right)\\[5pt] &= 2xy\sin{(x^2 - y^2)} \end{align}

To find $f_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $f_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} f_{yx}(x,y)&=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(f_y(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(-y\cos{(x^2- y^2)}\right) \\[5pt] &= -y\left(-\sin{(x^2 - y^2)}\cdot 2x\right) \\[5pt] &=2xy\sin{(x^2 - y^2)} \end{align}

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} f_{xy}(x,y) + f_{yx}(x,y) &= 2xy\sin{(x^2 - y^2)} + 2xy\sin{(x^2 - y^2)}\\[5pt] &= 4xy\sin{(x^2 - y^2)} . \end{align*}

question.text: Find $g_{xx}(x,y)+g_{yy}(x,y)$ at $(1,1)$ given that $g_x(x,y) = e^y + y e^x$ and $g_y(x,y) = x e^y + e^x.$
question.explanation:
To find $g_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $g_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} g_{xx}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left( g_x (x,y)\right) \\[3pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(e^y + y e^x\right)\\[3pt] &= 0+y e^x\\[3pt] &= ye^x \end{align}

To find $g_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $g_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} g_{yy}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left( g_y (x,y)\right) \\[3pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(x e^y + e^x\right)\\[3pt] &= x e^y +0\\[3pt] &= xe^y \end{align}

Next, we evaluate $g_{xx}(x,y)$ and $g_{yy}(x,y)$ at $(1,1)\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} g_{xx}(1,1) &= 1\cdot e^1 =e\\[5pt] g_{yy}(1,1) &= 1\cdot e^1 =e \end{align}

Finally, we have

\[g_{xx}(1,1)+g_{yy}(1,1)=e+e=2e .\]

Next, we find $g_{yy}(x,y)$ by differentiating $g_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} g_{yy}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(g_y(x,y) \right) \\[3pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left( \dfrac{x}{x+y} \right) \\[3pt] &=-\dfrac{x}{(x+y)^2} \end{align*}

Finally, we find $g_{yyx}(x,y)$ by differentiating $g_{yy}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} g_{yyx}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(g_{yy} (x,y)\right) \\[3pt] &=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(-\dfrac{x}{(x+y)^2}\right) \\[3pt] &=-\dfrac{1}{(x+y)^2}+\dfrac{2x}{(x+y)^3} \\[3pt] &=\dfrac{-(x+y)+2x}{(x+y)^3} \\[3pt] &=\dfrac{x-y}{(x+y)^3} \\[3pt] \end{align*}

\begin{align*} f_{x}(x,y,z) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left( x^2\ln(y+z) \right) \\[5pt] &= 2x\ln(y+z) \end{align*}

Now, we find $f_{xy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $f_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{xy}(x,y,z)&=\dfrac{\partial }{\partial y} \left(f_{x}(x,y,z) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left( 2x\ln(y+z) \right) \\[5pt] &= 2x\cdot \dfrac{1}{y+z} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2x}{y+z} \end{align*}

Next, we find $f_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $f_{xy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{xyz}(x,y,z) &=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial z} \left(f_{xy}(x,y,z) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial z} \left( \dfrac{2x}{y+z} \right) \\[5pt] &= 2x \cdot \dfrac {\partial }{\partial z} \left( \dfrac{1}{y+z} \right) \\[5pt] &= 2x \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{(y+z)^2} \right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{2x}{(y+z)^2} \end{align*}

Finally, we evaluate $f_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ at $(-5,2,3)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{xyz}(-5,2,3) &= -\dfrac{2(-5)}{(2+3)^2} = \dfrac{2}{5} \end{align*}

\begin{align*} f_{z}(x,y,z) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial z} \left( x^2z^3\sqrt{y}\right) \\[5pt] &= 3x^2z^2\sqrt{y} \end{align*}

Now, we find $f_{zy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $f_{z}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

Next, we find $f_{zyx}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $f_{zy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{zyx}(x,y,z) &=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(f_{zy}(x,y,z) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left( \dfrac{3x^2z^2}{2\sqrt{y}} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3xz^2}{\sqrt{y}} \end{align*}

Next, we find $f_{xx}(x,y)$ by differentiating $f_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$
